title: Determine Equivalent Ratios Using Graphs
objective: I can graph the values from a ratio table as points on the coordinate plane.
model: ordered pairs from a ratio table plotted on the coordinate plane, points on a line through the origin

widgets.component: 3-3 review: next row, row that does not belong, scale 3 eggs : 5 flour
widgets.root: Same ratio-table skills as 3-3; they build the pairs this lesson plots.

widgets.component: next ordered pair (8, 24); graph of equivalent ratios is a straight line through the origin; y when x = 7 is 28
adds 2 to 3 instead of multiplying to get an ordered pair (3, 5)
widgets.root: The first wrong step is flagged; fix (3, 6).

widgets.component: ratio of y to x is 4:1; whose line is steeper
fill-in table whose Ordered Pair cells are typed text
widgets.root: The y cells are numeric but the pair cells '(2, 10)', '(4, 20)', '(6, 30)' are graded by exact string (assets/studio/kinds-basic.js K.tbl), so '(2,10)' without the space, or '2, 10', is marked wrong.
widgets.replacement: Normalise ordered pairs in the grader (strip spaces, require parentheses) or drop the third column and ask the student to plot the rows with act:plot mode 'table'. Keep y as numbers.

widgets.component: errors on a graph, using the rule y = 4x
widgets.root: The step text and the fix use the equation y = 4x ('Using the rule y = 4x, when x = 4 the y-value must be 16'); the two-variable equation y = kx is first derived in 9-3, six lessons of Unit 9 away. In 3-4 the rule is the ratio table.
widgets.replacement: Rewrite without the equation: 'A recipe uses 4 cups of water for every 1 cup of rice. A student plots (1, 4), (2, 8), (3, 12) and (4, 14).' Fix: 'For 4 cups of rice the table gives 4 × 4 = 16 cups of water, so (4, 16) is on the line; (4, 14) is not.'

widgets.component: read a point's coordinates, the unit-rate point (1, k), which points share a ratio, do the points show equivalent ratios
widgets.root: Rendered the coordinate figure at L1 and L4: viewBox, axis labels and labelled points are present; the points sit at the stated coordinates; keys checked against y ÷ x.

widgets.component: plot each pair of a ratio table as a point
widgets.root: The lesson's model: the student plots (first quantity, second quantity) and sees the line through the origin; the only plotting task in Practice (every other graph item asks the student to read a graph or complete a table).

widgets.component: 'Why do the points form a straight line through (0, 0)?' and 'Which point would NOT be on this line?'
widgets.root: The food-truck scenario and its line are not in the stems: 5.2 says 'this line' with no line or ratio given, and 5.1's distractors mention tacos and salsa the student has never been told about.
widgets.replacement: Add the scenario and a figure: 'A food truck plots tacos sold (x) and ounces of salsa used (y): (1, 2), (2, 4), (3, 6), a line through (0, 0).' with viz {t:'coord', xmin:0, xmax:6, ymin:0, ymax:12, points:[(1,2),(2,4),(3,6)], line:{m:2,b:0}, xlabel:'Tacos', ylabel:'Ounces of salsa'}; 5.2 'Which point is NOT on this line?' keeps (5, 12).

which two points show equivalent ratios; line reading; which recipe matches the graph
widgets.root: Rendered and recomputed: A (5, 15) and C (1, 3) share 3; the L4 lines (slopes 5/6 and 2.5) match exactly one named recipe.

plot the table's points; blanks to fill first
widgets.root: Manipulable; L3-L4 require finding the missing table values before plotting.

widgets.where: Challenge §3 item 3.3 (sort of points by 'y = 2.5 × x')
widgets.component: stem states the equation y = 2.5 × x
widgets.root: The stem says 'its line follows y = 2.5 × x'; the equation form y = kx is taught in 9-3. The six cards themselves are fine (on the line: (4,10), (6,15), (10,25)).
widgets.replacement: Restate: 'A kitchen uses 5 cups of flour for every 2 loaves, which is 2.5 cups for 1 loaf. Sort each point (loaves, cups) by whether it is on that line.' Keep the cards.
